clue.text: Caught unawares, like a thief seized in an ambush?

definitions.meaning: surprised when not expecting anything, unprepared

definitions.text: like a thief seized in an ambush?
definitions.meaning: a thief grabbed by lurking police is literally captured by a sudden unexpected move

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: the thief is caught, and the catching is a surprise attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be startled by the unexpected is to be caught off guard, the plain sense of the first definition.

clue.text: Leaves Virginia, perhaps

parts.note: reads like someone departing a US state, but Virginia is a famous type of cured leaf for smoking

explanation.surface: Someone quits the state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure; it is the noun, the dried plant leaves, and Virginia is a classic variety of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a well-known variety of the cured leaf smoked in pipes and cigarettes.

clue.text: Kind of silk T shirts? No, other sorts of clothing

definitions.text: shirts? No, other sorts of clothing

indicators.note: a kind of something is a variant form, so the letters of silk and T are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether silk T-shirts are meant, and is told it is different garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges SILK plus the T of 'T shirts'; the rest of the clue, rejecting shirts, points to another garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilts are Scottish pleated skirt garments, an article of clothing that is plainly not a shirt.

clue.text: Opened cans in use, the pests!

indicators.note: cans that are opened have their contents broken out, so the letters of cans in use are spilled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about people opening tins that are in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened' signals the anagram of CANS INUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pests in the sense of annoying people or things are irritants and bothers.

clue.text: Seek any sort of name for the Americans!

indicators.note: a sort of something is a rough version of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look for some name or other to call the people of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the letters of SEEKANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A common, originally slightly mocking, nickname for people from the United States.

clue.text: Greek booked by Irishman

definitions.meaning: the Latin name of the Greek hero Odysseus of Homer's epic
a book written by an Irish author, here James Joyce's 1922 novel

explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce, an Irishman, gave his most famous novel the Latin name of Homer's wandering Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman form of Odysseus's name, and the title of James Joyce's celebrated Dublin novel.

clue.text: Used to stamp iron

definitions.meaning: a machine or tool that pushes down to impress a mark or shape
to smooth clothes with a hot iron

explanation.definitionFit: A press is a stamping machine, and to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot iron.

clue.text: Lack of interest in work-code Lenin organised

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Lenin drew up a labour code, which bred apathy about work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges CODELENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness, a disinclination to exert oneself, is the sense of the noun.

clue.text: Object to a smaller amount never stopping

parts.note: an object or aim is an end, as in 'to that end'
less means a smaller quantity

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a smaller quantity being provided all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest; it is the noun, a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without end continues for ever, without stopping.

clue.text: Stock market gambler-one with no change, either gold or silver

parts.note: a bull is a speculator who buys expecting prices to rise
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: changing the little word no switches its two letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: A speculator on the stock exchange, with no small change, must hold precious metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no change' reads as having no coins, but 'change' rearranges NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bulk, as bars or ingots, valued by weight.

clue.text: It's conceded to be lie Eddy circulated

indicators.note: letters sent circulating are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: It is admitted that a lie told by Eddy was spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' rearranges LIEEDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield a point in argument is to concede it, so both are past tense verbs of giving way.

clue.text: Lady of Spain played on them when music required!

definitions.text: Lady of Spain played on them when music required!

parts.words: Lady of Spain played on them when music required!
parts.note: suggests a song title being played, but describes the clicking wooden instruments a Spanish dancer holds

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman performs on some instrument whenever music is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady of Spain' is also the name of a popular song, which makes 'played' seem to be about a tune; the lady is a flamenco dancer clicking her instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-held pairs of wooden shells clicked together, associated with Spanish dance.

clue.text: Tortured slave gets ointment for his wounds

indicators.note: tortured means twisted and wrenched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slave who has been tortured is given soothing cream for his injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortured' rearranges SLAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a healing or soothing cream rubbed on wounds or sores.

clue.text: Said by clergymen to be areas of clerical endeavour

definitions.meaning: the daily services of prayer read by priests, the divine services
places where clerks do paperwork, workrooms

explanation.walkthrough: 'clerical' looks like it continues the clergy theme, but here it means office clerks' work.
explanation.definitionFit: Church services of daily prayer bear this name, and so do rooms where desk work is done.

clue.text: St Peter, if upset, going after US general

indicators.note: the general is placed after the overturned word
upset in a down clue means turned over, so the little word is read upwards

parts.note: William Tecumseh Sherman, Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Saint Peter, if annoyed, goes chasing an American general.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the little word upwards; Peter was a Galilean who fished for a living before following Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Apostle earned his living casting nets on the Sea of Galilee before becoming a disciple.

clue.text: Kept back money from wages, etc.

definitions.text: Kept back money from wages, etc.

parts.words: Kept back money from wages, etc.
parts.note: sounds like docking someone's pay, but describes cash put aside out of income

explanation.surface: An employer withholds part of a worker's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept back' suggests an employer withholding pay; it means money a person sets aside for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Money reserved rather than spent, put by from one's earnings for the future.

clue.text: Suggests highly portable device for those in distress

definitions.meaning: extremely easy to carry because it weighs so little
a coloured flare fired from a pistol as a signal, named after its inventor Edward Very

explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare fired from a Very pistol, named after the US naval officer who devised it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely weightless is easy to carry, and the Very flare signals that a ship or party needs help.

clue.text: Doctor dies on way to the Pole, so doesn't continue

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
S stands for south, one of the two poles

explanation.surface: A doctor dies on the journey towards the South Pole, so the expedition ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person who dies, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of DIES and ST, which gives DESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or stop doing something, so it means refrains from carrying on.

clue.text: Poured on oil, and applied bandages

definitions.meaning: put an oil-based dressing over a salad
covered a wound with gauze and bandage

explanation.definitionFit: A salad is dressed with oil and vinegar, and a wound is dressed with bandages.

clue.text: Player-a reserve

definitions.meaning: an actor or performer who takes another's part
a substitute kept ready to step in

explanation.definitionFit: An understudy or substitute who replaces an absent performer or team member.

clue.text: Oriental people submerge Gurkha leader going adrift

indicators.note: adrift means wandering loose, so the remaining letters drift into a new order
the Gurkha's first letter is going, taken out of the word submerge
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Eastern people sink a Gurkha commander and leave him floating.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the G of 'Gurkha' (its 'leader') from SUBMERGE leaves SUBMERE, which 'adrift' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Burma (Myanmar) in South-East Asia, once loosely called Oriental.

clue.text: A cleaner W. Country community but backward.

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, in the West Country of England

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word but from right to left

explanation.surface: A cleaner from a West Country town, though somewhat slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; Bath is its famous spa city. 'backward' looks like it describes a slow-witted cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tub one sits in to wash, so a means of getting clean.

clue.text: … and German town after a couple of bridge players-old Jews

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, Germany
East and South are two of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Continuing a list: a German town, then two card players, then some ancient Jews.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so two of them are E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect around the time of Christ, linked with the Dead Sea Scrolls.

clue.text: Levels the odds

definitions.meaning: makes flat or equal, as in levelling the score
betting odds of one to one

explanation.definitionFit: To even something is to make it level, and even money is a one-to-one betting price.

clue.text: Saracen chief drops in for something cool to eat

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so the little word is removed from the chief's name

parts.note: Saladin was the Muslim sultan who fought the Crusaders

explanation.surface: The Saracen leader stops by for a chilled snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like 'visits', but 'drops' removes IN from SALADIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold dish of raw vegetables or leaves is the classic chilled food.

clue.text: Hill-dweller runs off and marries deer!

parts.note: ants live in anthills
to elope is to run away secretly to marry

explanation.surface: Someone from the hills runs away to wed a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill-dweller' suggests a mountain person, but it is the insect of the anthill.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are swift, horned grazing animals loosely likened to deer, here used broadly.

clue.text: Favourite the Frenchwoman backed makes it a bit of a bloomer

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: The favourite was backed by the Frenchwoman, which proved a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake or a bet that went wrong, but here it is a flower; 'backed' looks like a punter backing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is literally something that blooms, a flower, and a petal is one piece of it.

clue.text: Tried a quarter-quite enough for old copper

parts.note: S is south, one of the four quarters of the compass
ample means plenty, more than enough
d was the symbol for a penny, a copper coin, in pre-1971 British money

explanation.surface: Someone tried a quarter and found that enough for a former policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; it is a penny, d in old British money.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample something is to try or taste a little of it.

clue.text: A great man, it's said, to put a stop to slackness

definitions.text: to put a stop to slackness

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word for a great man is heard rather than written

parts.note: a titan is a person of great stature or importance

explanation.surface: A great man is reportedly needed to end the laxity.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a rope taut removes its slack, and stricter rules remove laxness.

clue.text: In which we throw bell, punches?

definitions.text: In which we throw bell, punches?

parts.words: In which we throw bell, punches?
parts.note: pictures fights with bells and blows, describing hard-fought contests full of back-and-forth exchanges

explanation.surface: A scene where people hurl a bell and swing punches.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxing match runs between rings of the bell; 'ding-dong' is the bell's sound and an idiom for a lively, evenly matched fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: fiercely contested, evenly matched struggles with blows traded back and forth.
